title.purpose: Entry headings such as a job or a project.

meta.purpose: Place and date lines, menu bar text.

terminal.purpose: Terminal output and the boot log.

shadows.name: window-rest

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve: window open and close, press feedback.

motion.name: window-open
motion.purpose: Opacity 0 to 1 and scale 0.96 to 1, growing from the icon that opened the window.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Scale to 0.97 on file icons and the button, 0.9 on the close button.

motion.name: button-colour
motion.purpose: Background and text colour change on the primary button.

motion.name: boot-lines
motion.purpose: Delays at which the four boot log lines appear, each instantly.

motion.name: boot-out
motion.purpose: Fade-out of the boot screen. Once per session; any click or key skips it.

motion.name: start-stagger
motion.purpose: On wide desktops the terminal opens first and about.md follows.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No boot sequence, no scale, no press transitions, no smooth scrolling. Windows still fade.

narrative.overview:
The site is a small operating system, not a page. The wallpaper is flat electric orange. The content sits in cream windows with a thin dark outline, and each window is a file with its name in the title bar. One window, the terminal, is dark. On small or touch screens, and without JavaScript, the same windows stack into one readable column.

The system shares its tokens with a sister site (cream, coffee ink, orange, 12px corners, Bricolage Grotesque headings, system sans body). The difference is that orange is the ground here, not an accent. Everything else is quiet: flat fills, 1px lines, two soft shadows, and very little motion.
keyCharacteristics: Flat orange ground, cream windows, one dark terminal.
1px lines and 12px corners. No gradients, no pills.
Three type voices: Bricolage Grotesque for headings, system sans for reading, mono for filenames and the terminal.
Two layouts from one HTML source: a desktop with draggable windows, and a stacked page.
Motion is short and rare: one boot sequence, then quick window opens and closes.

rules.name: The Orange Ground Rule
rules.body: Orange is the wallpaper. On cream it appears only as the one button fill and as an underline colour.

rules.name: The No Orange Text On Cream Rule
rules.body: Orange on cream is 3.3:1, too low for text. Text on cream uses Rust Link or Coffee Ink. Orange text is allowed on the terminal ground (5.6:1). Text on orange is always Coffee Ink (5.4:1).

rules.name: The One Dark Window Rule
rules.body: Only the terminal and the boot screen use the terminal colours. Everything else is cream.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is for the name, window titles, entry titles and the "TORRES OS" brand. Mono is for filenames, the terminal and the boot log. Everything else is system sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: The clock and the year column use tabular figures so they do not shift.

rules.name: The Front Window Rule
rules.body: The active window is shown in three ways at once: the deeper shadow, a tinted title bar (Soft Canvas, or Terminal Bar), and a title in full ink. Windows behind it have a title bar in their body colour and a muted title.

rules.name: The Shadows Mean Stacking Rule
rules.body: A shadow says that one thing lies on top of another. Nothing on the stacked page, the menu bar or the buttons has one.

dos: Do keep orange as the ground and put content in cream windows.
Do put Coffee Ink on orange for all text and icons on the wallpaper.
Do give every new piece of content its own window with a filename, a file icon and an entry in the terminal, read from the same HTML.
Do use 1px lines: ink for outlines, Hairline for dividers inside a window.
Do keep hover styles inside `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.
Do make sure new content also works on the stacked page and without JavaScript.
Do keep window motion at 180ms to open and 120ms to close, with a reduced-motion version that only fades.
donts: Don't use orange for text on cream. Use Rust Link.
Don't add a second dark surface. The terminal and the boot screen are the only ones.
Don't use gradients, pills or fully round corners.
Don't add shadows on the stacked page, or to buttons and the menu bar.
Don't use mono type outside filenames, the terminal and the boot log.
Don't add scroll animations, looping animations or a second intro. The boot sequence is the only staged motion.
Don't put cards inside windows. Separate entries with a Hairline rule.
